title: Security, Privacy & Responsible AI
description: Recognize trust boundaries, protect credentials and data, validate inputs and permissions, assess dependencies, and use model outputs responsibly.

lessons.title: Threat modeling for beginners
lessons.principle: A threat model identifies valuable assets, actors, entry points, trust boundaries, and plausible abuse.
lessons.practice: Trace user data from browser to API to storage and note who controls each step.

lessons.title: Rate risk by consequence
lessons.principle: A public theme selector and a billing or identity endpoint require different security depth.
lessons.practice: Prioritize authorization, sensitive-data flows, destructive actions, and externally reachable services.

lessons.title: Input validation and injection
lessons.principle: Untrusted input must not be interpreted as code, commands, SQL, or markup without safe handling.
lessons.practice: Prefer parameterized database queries and APIs that distinguish data from executable syntax.

lessons.title: Protect the browser too
lessons.principle: Rendering untrusted text as HTML can execute hostile content in a user's session.
lessons.practice: Use textContent for ordinary user strings and established safe rendering for intentional rich content.

lessons.title: Identity, sessions, and permissions
lessons.principle: A session conveys authenticated identity, but every protected operation still needs authorization.
lessons.practice: Test that user A cannot edit user B's task by changing an identifier.

lessons.title: Fail closed at the boundary
lessons.principle: UI hiding, client-supplied owner IDs, and model-generated permission logic are not sufficient enforcement.
lessons.practice: Derive the actor identity from verified server-side context and check ownership on each operation.

lessons.title: Secrets and least privilege
lessons.principle: Credentials must be stored securely and given only the capabilities required for their purpose.
lessons.practice: Use separate local, test, and production credentials with narrow scopes.

lessons.title: Review AI tool permissions
lessons.principle: A coding assistant with unrestricted filesystem, terminal, network, and deployment access has a large blast radius.
lessons.practice: Limit tool actions, review proposed commands, and require approval for production or destructive operations.

lessons.title: Dependencies and supply chain
lessons.principle: Third-party packages, build actions, and downloaded scripts can introduce defects or malicious behavior.
lessons.practice: Inspect new dependencies and pin appropriate versions when reproducibility matters.

lessons.title: Do not blindly trust generated imports
lessons.principle: AI may suggest an obsolete API or a package with a similar name to a popular library.
lessons.practice: Confirm package identity, provenance, maintenance, vulnerabilities, and license before adding it.

lessons.title: Privacy and data minimization
lessons.principle: Collect, retain, display, and transmit only information necessary for the approved task.
lessons.practice: Use synthetic data in learning examples and define retention expectations.

lessons.title: Keep private data out of prompts
lessons.principle: Model prompts, logs, transcripts, and tool calls may cross organizational boundaries.
lessons.practice: Remove credentials and personal records before sharing context with external AI services.

lessons.title: Prompt injection awareness
lessons.principle: Instructions embedded in repository files, search results, web pages, or model outputs may conflict with the user's real task.
lessons.practice: Treat retrieved content as data and maintain the authorized task boundary.

lessons.title: Guard agent instructions
lessons.principle: A README comment or issue body should not be allowed to override approval, secrecy, or write-access rules.
lessons.practice: Review untrusted instructions and require explicit authorized confirmation for unrelated tool actions.

lessons.title: AI outputs and intellectual property
lessons.principle: Generated material may contain incorrect claims, incompatible licenses, or patterns copied without adequate review.
lessons.practice: Check attribution, license obligations, and organization policy for incorporated assets or code.

lessons.title: Keep human accountability
lessons.principle: A model's recommendation does not replace engineering review or legal and domain-specific judgment.
lessons.practice: Document sources when needed and have a responsible reviewer approve consequential use.

lessons.title: Failure-safe product behavior
lessons.principle: Features using an external model should handle timeout, unavailable service, invalid output, and budget exhaustion.
lessons.practice: Define fallback behavior that preserves core user tasks where possible.

lessons.title: Validate structured model output
lessons.principle: Model-produced JSON can be malformed or semantically invalid even when formatted confidently.
lessons.practice: Parse against a schema, reject unauthorized fields, and never directly execute model-produced commands.

lessons.title: Accessibility and broader impact
lessons.principle: Quality includes making software usable across different abilities, devices, languages, and connectivity conditions.
lessons.practice: Test focus, contrast, plain-language messages, and offline or poor-network recovery.

lessons.title: Check who a feature excludes
lessons.principle: An AI-centric workflow can disadvantage users unable to access paid models or fast networks.
lessons.practice: Keep essential product functions usable without mandatory AI when appropriate and document limitations.
